executiveSummary: GM0302's official 2025 identity, contained reference point, 29,393-resident control, fourteen neighbourhoods, four BAG places, eight BRT settlements and five logical road-border links are coherent, and all ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Nunspeet extends from Veluwemeer/Randmeren lowlands across the Veluwe flank to extensive forest and heath around Elspeet and Vierhouten. The canonical major-river preset reports an exact persistent 1.662487 m depth, 438 affected residents and 284,425 person-hours at T+24, rising to 459 and 1,119,309 at T+72, without a selected IJssel or connected local pathway. The narrow direct North Sea coastal result of zero depth is reasonable only for that source; it does not establish safety from Veluwemeer/Randmeren high water, streams, groundwater or drainage. Municipal evidence explicitly distinguishes the Veluwe groundwater-fluctuation zone, absent or present drainage, rainfall infiltration/storage, drought and urban wastewater. At audit time the water board reported regional crisis phase 2 for drought, groundwater well below seasonal normal and abstraction restrictions, but this regional timestamped context is neither a Nunspeet measurement nor automatically scenario forcing. Nature fire is the clearest contradiction. VNOG's 2025–2028 profile assigns 8,487 ha of nature to Nunspeet, cites real Elspeet and A28/Hulshorst fires and models smoke over campsites, roads and villages with insufficiently self-reliant camping/nature visitors. The simulator's canonical wildfire reports flame 0.116907, smoke 0.485399 and zero affected residents. Moving the source into the 3,770 ha Vierhouten forest neighbourhood raises flame to 0.462991 and smoke to 0.535965 but still affects nobody; the unchanged shared hazard order ranks resident-heavy Nunspeet-West first and the source area fourth. Historical municipal tourism evidence reports 810,300 taxable overnight stays in 2018, 56 holiday parks/campsites and 14 hotels, while explicitly excluding some second-home stays; none of this dynamic occupancy enters the 29,393-resident denominator. A28 is one series corridor toward Elburg and Harderwijk, N310 one cross-Veluwe route toward Elburg/Apeldoorn, and Nunspeet station/rail can be exposed by fire, smoke, trees, power and access conditions; St Jansdal acute care is external in Harderwijk. Public context supplies 34 partial water assets, one electricity planning sample, provider polygons, 77 antenna sites and 25 education locations but no local Waterinfo, fixed KNMI, RIVM air, NDW or acute-care point. These records do not supply live topology, capacity, backup, staffing, occupancy, outage or restoration. Exact first-72-hour hazard, service, route and recovery values must remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until incident-specific forcing, dynamic population, physical dependencies and confirmed actions/resources are bound; NoData is never zero, open, safe or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0302 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0302 as Nunspeet in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland, with 29,393 residents, density 228/km², 21.9% aged 65 or older and 3,434 one-person households. The reference point [5.779761415961549,52.33321551805701] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Fourteen neighbourhoods in two districts sum to 29,380 residents, thirteen below the municipal control (-0.044%); households total 11,675 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 6,445. Deterministic allocation adds thirteen without rewriting observations.

Elspeet, Hulshorst, Nunspeet and Vierhouten are the four BAG places. Eight BRT settlements comprise three buurtschappen, one deelkern and four woonkernen; no place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.
Cars per household is null in one neighbourhood; district-heating and public-charging fields are null in all fourteen. Null remains NoData, not numeric zero or service absence.

Large urban neighbourhoods Nunspeet-West/Oost and large sparse forest/rural neighbourhoods require different hazard and dynamic-occupancy evidence; resident totals alone cannot supply that distinction.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Nunspeet, gemeenten Hattem/Oldebroek/Elburg and Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Beleids- en beheerplan Water en Riolering
evidenceSources.edition: Joint policy/management plan published in 2023-era municipal records; planning and asset-management context, not an event-state feed; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The plan treats wastewater, rainwater, groundwater and surface water as connected but separately governed chains and records local water storage under the Dorpskerk parking area in Elspeet.

It identifies the Veluwe groundwater-fluctuation zone: future/high multiyear groundwater can create water nuisance especially on the flank where adequate streams, ditches or drainage are absent, while central-Veluwe groundwater can be very deep.

The strategy retains area water and infiltrates disconnected rainwater to reduce both drought and temporary excess; wastewater, rain infiltration, surface-water management and groundwater used for drinking water remain distinct.

The document says not all risk-dialogue results were available in time for the plan. Policy and investment intent are not a complete current pluvial/groundwater surface, asset state or performance guarantee.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, bijlagenboek natuurbrand
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk-profile period 2025–2028; official scenario/planning evidence, not an incident perimeter or live resource state; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: VNOG records 8,487 ha/84.87 km² of nature within Nunspeet and 56,423 ha on the Veluwe within the region. It cites a 2018 heath fire at Hooiweg Elspeet and 2022 heath/forest fires along A28 at Hulshorst and Beekhuizerzand.
Its scenario uses running fire in inaccessible conifer forest and heath, a 1.5–2.5 km² fire and 5.5–6.5 km² smoke area affecting nature, campsites, motorway and villages.

Camping and nature-area visitors are identified as insufficiently self-reliant; the scenario links high holiday pressure, dry intake points, low groundwater, inadequate extinguishing water, difficult fireground access and rapid spread.

The current public nature-fire-risk page displayed phase 1 for Noord- en Oost-Gelderland at audit time. That regional daily status means no extra measures at that time, not zero Nunspeet fuel, zero ignition probability, a T+72 forecast or safety.
Regional scenario dimensions demonstrate plausible mechanisms and response concerns but are not a local forecast, selected Nunspeet ignition, evacuation order or proof of available crews/water.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Actueel waterbeeld and water-level/groundwater management
evidenceSources.edition: Water-board situation page last updated 2 September 2026 at 13:58 local time; regional timestamped observation/decision context; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The authority reported drought not over, groundwater well below seasonal normal, fragile surface-water recovery and an average management-area precipitation deficit near 250 mm. Local conditions and discharges vary by area.

It reported its crisis organization in phase 2 and surface-water abstraction bans plus groundwater-abstraction bans near vulnerable streams and wet nature. These are current regional measures, not automatic Nunspeet service percentages.
Groundwater recovers more slowly than surface water and requires longer precipitation; this contradicts any generic assumption that forcing clearance establishes water-system recovery.

The board uses pumps/weirs and groundwater gauges for wet/dry management and can deviate from normal target levels in exceptional conditions; no inspected public record supplies a full live GM0302 catchment/control state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Monitor toerisme en recreatie Nunspeet 2018/2019
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal factsheet published 2020, reporting 2018 statistics and a 2019 enterprise survey; historic context, blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The monitor reports 810,300 tourist-tax overnight stays in 2018, explicitly excluding forensenbelasting stays, plus 56 holiday parks/campsites, fourteen hotels, eight bed-and-breakfast businesses and three group accommodations.
It reports 1,180 tourism/recreation jobs and notes part-time, full-time and temporary workers; these historic figures are not a current employee roster or incident-time occupancy.
The earlier municipal audit says holiday-park supply makes total recreational-destination nights probably materially higher than taxable-night counts because some second-home stays are excluded.
Annual nights, establishment counts, beds and historic jobs cannot be converted into people present at T0–T+72; current registered and estimated visitor/worker occupancy remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Veluwemeer/Randmeren, A28 and completed Nunspeet station-area works
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS water/road pages and ProRail completion notice dated 20 March 2026, inspected 3 September 2026; infrastructure context, blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: RWS identifies Veluwemeer as a Randmeer, approximately 30 km² and -3.00 m NAP, created beside old land and part of a recreational route. It is not the North Sea and not a canonical direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel source.

A28 is one physical corridor toward Harderwijk and Elburg/Oldebroek; RWS publishes current/lifecycle traffic information, but NWB edge values do not establish vehicles/hour, emergency access, smoke visibility or evacuation throughput.

ProRail says the renewed Nunspeet station area opened 20 March 2026 after replacing Elspeterweg's level crossing with separate road and cycle/pedestrian underpasses and improving the station. Completed infrastructure is not proof of incident-time passability or rail service.

N310's two municipality edges are series directions of one cross-Veluwe regional corridor, while N795 connects toward Epe. None is guaranteed independent during fire, fallen trees, snow, flood, congestion or closure.
Rail, A28, N310, local forest roads and Veluwemeer recreation require separate mode, structure, issue/valid time and operating state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland and Ziekenhuis St Jansdal
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Regionaal Crisisplan 2025–2028 and external emergency care
evidenceSources.edition: Crisis plan adopted 12 December 2024 for 2025–2028; St Jansdal current public department page inspected 3 September 2026; doctrine/facility context, not an incident resource commitment
supports: The crisis plan requires large-scale alerting to start within two minutes after criteria are met and defines current command, information, public-care, mobility, medical, fire/emission and recovery responsibilities.
Public care plans, executes, monitors and adjusts moving, sheltering and caring for people; these are roles, not proof of current sites, occupancy, transport, staff, stock or completion.

St Jansdal says its Harderwijk emergency department is open day and night. RIVM v1.1 reports it as 24/7 with acute obstetrics, eighteen treatment rooms and 24,660 2025 visits; it lies outside GM0302 about 11.2 km straight-line from the reference point.
Neither source establishes A28/local access, ambulance availability, staffing, generator/fuel, diversion, live capacity or acceptance for a selected Nunspeet event.
A doctrine milestone must not change service availability unless an incident actor, action, resource, location, valid time and confirmation are recorded.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis, Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RIVM, RDI, DUO, KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial water, utility, telecom, education, care, weather and traffic context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026, CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness; other deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026 with source-specific editions/licences
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns 34 HWH objects: five sewer pumps with non-null capacity numbers and 29 weirs with null capacity. Named pumps include Hulshorst, Elspeet, Vierhouten and two Nunspeet buffers; no contained surface-water pump, sluice or treatment plant is proof of absence from the functional chain.

One 8071XJ sample maps to Liander area OS Nunspeet 10-1i and reports 32/28 MW existing/required withdrawal, a 5.8 MW/19-request queue, 32/11 MW injection, 28 projects and earliest 2029. It is large-user planning context, not current load, outage or reserve.

At the reference point public polygons return Liander for power/gas, Vitens for drinking water, Ziggo for media and no drainage match. Provider areas are responsibility context, not connectivity, topology, pressure, coverage quality or restoration.
RDI assigns 77 sites/175 antennas and DUO 25 education locations. Registers do not establish radio coverage/backhaul/power, occupancy, shelter designation, staff or stock.

Zero contained Waterinfo observation/forecast, fixed KNMI observation/warning, RIVM PM2.5/acute-care, government-service, NDW-situation and recent seismic points are scoped NoData, never normal conditions, open routes, available services or safety.

identity.summary: GM0302, Nunspeet, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland agree across generated and official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature ID, bundle code/name, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized 2025 geometry and all four BAG label points are contained.
Administrative edition, historic/current policy, timestamped situation, official scenario and synthetic exercise time remain separate.

geography.summary: Veluwemeer-to-Veluwe context is strong, but generalized geometry is not a hydraulic, groundwater, fuel or access surface.
notes: Veluwemeer/Randmeren high water, flank streams/groundwater, urban rain and deep dry Veluwe ground are distinct mechanisms.
Four forest/rural neighbourhoods each exceed 1,000 ha, but their administrative polygons do not encode vegetation, paths, fire breaks, occupants or response access.
Use full-resolution authority hydrology/elevation and current fuel/land-use/incident geometry for consequences.

demography.summary: Registered residents reconcile, but tourism and nature-area occupancy can vary sharply and is absent.
notes: Published neighbourhood population is 29,380, thirteen below the 29,393 control (-0.044%); deterministic reconciliation adds thirteen.
Historic 810,300 taxable overnight stays and 56 holiday parks/campsites establish material seasonal exposure, not present people.
Registered residents, accommodation guests, second-home users, day visitors, workers, responders and care-dependent groups require separate timestamped cohorts.

regionalDetail.summary: All fourteen neighbourhoods are retained, but resident weighting misrepresents sparse forests, campsites and route exposure.
notes: Nunspeet-West/Oost contain 18,370 published residents; bosgebied Vierhouten contains 300 across 3,770 ha and Elspeetse Bos 115 across 2,151 ha.
Low registered population does not mean low fire/smoke, visitor, road or response exposure.
Null district-heating/charging and one cars-per-household value remain NoData.

settlements.summary: Four BAG places and eight BRT settlements preserve urban, village and small-settlement context without containment mismatch.
notes: BRT types are three buurtschappen, one deelkern and four woonkernen.
Settlement labels provide identity, not resident/visitor occupancy, evacuation direction or shelter role.
Elspeet and Vierhouten require forest-interface and seasonal context despite small resident totals.

transport.summary: Five logical road links omit common corridors, rail and incident-specific rural/care continuity.
notes: A28's Elburg and Harderwijk edges are series directions of one corridor; N310's Elburg and Apeldoorn edges are another series corridor and must not add as independent capacity.
Nunspeet station and 37 transit stop areas are infrastructure/schedules, not trains, buses, drivers, smoke-safe routes or evacuation capacity.
St Jansdal care, mutual aid and supply depend on A28/local roads; forest access and traffic can be jointly impaired by fire/smoke, weather, trees or closures.

emergencyContext.summary: Current doctrine and official nature-fire scenario define decisions, but T0–T+72 sites/resources/actions remain Unknown.
notes: Fire scenario decisions require current ignition/perimeter, wind, fuel moisture, visitors, campgrounds, road/access, extinguishing-water and suppression resources.
Regional drought phase 2 at audit time is timestamped context, not permission to infer local drinking-water outage or fire behavior.
Shelter, evacuation, hospital acceptance, generators/fuel, distribution, crews, repair and restoration require confirmation rather than doctrine.

notes: Initial focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 31.45 seconds, tests 31.21 seconds.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, resident/demand/delivery reconciliation, determinism and cumulative-burden invariants hold for the resident-only model.
notes: All numeric outputs are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and never exceeds the fixed 29,393 resident control.
Neighbourhood residents and service demand/delivery sums reconcile at every frame.
This invariant excludes visitors/workers and does not validate physical capacity or displayed decimal precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared fourteen-neighbourhood order replaces hydrology, fuel, plume, weather, infrastructure and cyber geography.
notes: Eight nonzero single-hazard families have the identical local hazard order: Nunspeet-West, Vierhouten, Nunspeet-Zuid, bosgebied Vierhouten, then Elspeet, despite unrelated mechanisms.
A controlled ignition within bosgebied Vierhouten retains that order, ranks the source fourth and keeps affected population zero everywhere.
River allocation follows the same order and assigns upland Vierhouten second rather than using a selected Randmeren/stream/groundwater pathway.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability omits water-chain, forest access, rail/roads, external care and operator state.
notes: Thirty-four partial HWH assets do not drive sewers, groundwater, streams, weirs, wastewater treatment, drinking water or firefighting-water state.
One road-derived graph cannot model A28/N310 series constraints, rail, forest paths, smoke visibility, fallen trees, buses, ambulances and St Jansdal acceptance.
Provider polygons, one planning sample, antenna/school registers and an external hospital record do not calibrate live capacity, backup, outage or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers reconcile, but local causal provenance does not support the hazard and service precision.
notes: Hazard/service contribution sums and counterfactual records remain inspectable.
Wildfire T+24 reports flame 0.116907, smoke 0.485399, zero affected and 65,343 person-hours; controlled forest ignition raises forcing without source-contained exposure.
Earthquake has zero local motion/severity/affected but 24,369 person-hours at T+24 and 44,549 at T+72; label this an indirect synthetic network effect, not local earthquake damage.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 clearance, persistence and service changes are not driven by confirmed local actions or resources.
notes: Pluvial depth changes 0.405082→0 and burden 122,314→288,181 while services recover without rainfall, sewer, infiltration, stream, groundwater or clearance action.
Wildfire flame/smoke/affected change 0.116907/0.485399/0→0/0/0 while burden grows 65,343→254,042 without perimeter, suppression, evacuation, road or re-entry record.
Compound depth remains 0.418082 and affected rises 1,210→1,337 while burden grows 328,473→1,249,259 and services mostly freeze; no actor/resource causes the trajectory.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, containment, regional membership and resident reconciliation are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 plus audit:context verify GM0302/Nunspeet/Gelderland/VNOG, all place centres, the contained reference point and a thirteen-resident (-0.044%) rounding difference reconciled deterministically.
findings.action: Retain the 2025 edition, exact nulls, deterministic reconciliation and separate BAG/BRT semantics.

findings.summary: The canonical major-river preset asserts unsupported persistent Nunspeet inundation.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports depth 1.662487 and severity 0.526464 with affected 438→459 and burden 284,425→1,119,309. E02/E06 establish Veluwemeer/Randmeren, flank groundwater/streams and drainage, not a selected direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel event.
findings.action: Suppress direct canonical major-river consequence for GM0302; preserve selected Randmeren backwater/defence, local stream, groundwater and indirect supply pathways as Unknown until authority hydraulic evidence is bound.

findings.summary: Narrow North Sea coastal zero needs explicit scope so it does not imply Randmeren safety.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports depth/affected zero and 17,857 person-hours. E06 identifies Veluwemeer as a Randmeer; E02 separates surface, rain and groundwater systems. No selected Randmeren level, wind setup, defence, overtopping or lowland footprint exists.
findings.action: Retain exact direct North Sea zero only with source label; add a separately selected Veluwemeer/Randmeren event with level/datum, wind, boundary, defence, footprint and valid time, otherwise keep Unknown.

findings.summary: Generic depth collapses rainfall, urban sewer/storage, flank groundwater, streams and drought.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 has rain zero, depth 0.405082, zero affected and 122,314 person-hours; severe storm retains 0.371681 m after rain/wind zero. E02 describes the groundwater-fluctuation zone and water retention/infiltration; E04 records current regional drought phase 2.
findings.action: Bind event rain and groundwater to AHN/BGT, soils, catchments/streams, sewer/storage/outfalls and current initial state; treat drought, drinking water, wastewater and flood depth as distinct.

findings.summary: Wildfire reports nobody affected even for a controlled ignition inside extensive official Veluwe forest.
findings.evidence: E03 records 8,487 ha nature, local historic fires and camping/road/village smoke exposure. Canonical wildfire gives flame 0.116907/smoke 0.485399/affected zero; controlled bosgebied Vierhouten ignition gives 0.462991/0.535965 yet zero affected everywhere.
findings.action: Use eligible combustible-area/fuel/moisture, source/perimeter, wind/plume, dynamic occupancy, escape/access, water and suppression inputs; require source/adjacent consequence before unrelated areas and do not equate zero resident threshold with no people exposed.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active single hazards and the controlled fire reuse one exact neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Nunspeet-West, Vierhouten, Nunspeet-Zuid, bosgebied Vierhouten, Elspeet first-to-fifth. Moving ignition into bosgebied Vierhouten leaves it fourth.
findings.action: Replace shared seeded local severity with evidence-backed hydraulic, groundwater, urban-rain, wind, heat, fuel/fire, plume and cyber surfaces and test source containment and mechanism-specific rank divergence.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure omits large, fire-relevant seasonal and recreation populations.
findings.evidence: E05 reports 810,300 taxable nights in 2018, 56 holiday parks/campsites and fourteen hotels and says some second-home stays are excluded; E03 explicitly classifies camping/nature visitors as insufficiently self-reliant. Model exposure is capped at 29,393 residents.
findings.action: Add timestamped registered guests, estimated excluded/day/nature visitors, workers and responders as separate non-double-counted cohorts with uncertainty; never substitute annual nights, business count or beds for live occupancy.

findings.summary: A28/N310, rail, forest-road evacuation and external St Jansdal care are not operationally represented.
findings.evidence: E03 links fire/smoke to motorway, campsites and hard-to-access terrain. E06 shows A28/N310 series corridors and a completed station underpass, while E07 locates 24/7 acute care outside in Harderwijk. The five-edge graph has no rail, structure, smoke/tree, traffic, ambulance or hospital-acceptance state.
findings.action: Model physical corridors/structures and modes once with issue/valid state; route evacuation, mutual aid, rail/bus, supply and hospital transfer with direction, congestion, vehicle/crew and destination acceptance, else Unknown.

findings.summary: Partial water assets and provider/planning context cannot calibrate exact eight-service availability.
findings.evidence: E08 exposes five sewer pumps, 29 weirs, Liander/Vitens/Ziggo responsibility, one capacity-planning sample, antennas and schools, but no connected sewers/streams/WWTP, live load/pressure/quality, coverage/backhaul, backup, stock, crews or restoration.
findings.action: Label percentages synthetic; integrate only authorised, timestamped aggregate operational data and authority-reviewed hydrology, preserving partial registers, sensitive topology and null/no-match as Unknown.

findings.summary: Sparse/absent local observation coverage and regional status need explicit scope and time semantics.
findings.evidence: E04 is a 2 September management-area drought record whose local conditions vary. E08 has zero contained Waterinfo, KNMI, RIVM air/care, NDW and seismic points. Absence is not zero rain/water/fire/traffic/service or safety.
findings.action: Display publisher/version/licence, observation versus forecast/scenario/planning class, location, issue/valid/expiry time, units/datum, quality and coverage; keep NoData, Unknown, modeled zero and not applicable distinct.

findings.summary: First-72-hour hazard clearance and service trajectories lack confirmed actions, resources and blockers.
findings.evidence: Pluvial depth clears while burden grows 122,314→288,181; wildfire flame/smoke clears while burden grows 65,343→254,042; compound depth persists while burden grows 328,473→1,249,259. E07 supplies responsibilities, not event actions or completion.
findings.action: Add a T0/6/12/24/48/72 incident/action/resource/blocker ledger with actor, request/confirmation/dispatch/active/completion, location, capacity, dependency, valid/expiry time and uncertainty; suppress unconfirmed recovery attribution.

findings.summary: Exact map values can visually outrank older planning, current regional status and partial context without a release gate.
findings.evidence: Model outputs use six decimals and exact people/person-hours while E02/E03/E05 are planning/historic scenario context, E04 is timestamped regional status and E08 is partial/non-causal. No local calibration supports the visual precision.
findings.action: Gate operational display/export on event/source/time/coverage class; visibly badge Synthetic, Official scenario, Observation, Forecast, Planning, Unknown and NoData and suppress unsupported local decimals.
